paragraphs.title: The Return with Zerubbabel and the Family List

easy.explanation: They came up out of the captivity and had been carried away unto Babylon.
easy.q: From where did the people return to Jerusalem and Judah?

easy.explanation: Ezra says they came with Zerubbabel.
easy.q: Who was named among the leaders of the returning people?

easy.explanation: The passage lists families, places, and the number of people.
easy.q: What does the list mainly record?

answers: To show where the returnees came from
To name the kings of Israel
medium.explanation: The list identifies people by family and by place.
medium.q: Why are both families and localities mentioned?

answers: Each person returned to his city
medium.explanation: The returnees came again to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his city.
medium.q: What does “every one unto his city” mean?

medium.explanation: The numbers show that the returning community was counted carefully.
medium.q: What do the many numbers show about the return?

answers: The opening introduces all the returnees, and the list details them
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes the return generally and then names the groups.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the opening statement and the list that follows?

answers: Places as well as families are named
challenge.explanation: The list includes groups identified by cities and other localities.
challenge.q: Which detail could easily be overlooked in the family list?

answers: A census of the returning Israelites
challenge.explanation: It introduces the numbered list of the people and their families.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “the number of the men of the people of Israel” introduce?

easy.explanation: The section begins, “The priests.”
easy.q: Which group is listed first in this section?

easy.explanation: The passage lists priests, Levites, and singers.
easy.q: Who are listed with the priests?

easy.explanation: The text gives family names and the number of people in the groups.
easy.q: What information is given about these groups?

answers: It identifies groups serving the community and Temple
It describes the building of city walls
medium.explanation: The passage distinguishes priests, Levites, and singers by their service.
medium.q: What purpose does this section serve?

medium.explanation: The singers were associated with musical service.
medium.q: What does “the singers” refer to?

answers: To document the size of each group
medium.explanation: The numbers are part of the census of those who returned.
medium.q: Why are the numbers of each group recorded?

answers: The groups are presented according to distinct community roles
All the groups were one family
challenge.explanation: The passage separates groups according to their functions.
challenge.q: What does the order of the section suggest?

answers: Each group begins with its own designation
challenge.explanation: The text uses headings such as “The priests,” “The Levites,” and “The singers.”
challenge.q: What wording marks the different groups?

answers: All are counted as part of the returning community
The Levites and singers are not counted
challenge.explanation: All three groups are included among those who came up.
challenge.q: What relationship do the priests, Levites, and singers have in this list?

easy.explanation: The passage first lists the children of the porters.
easy.q: Which group is listed at the beginning of this section?

easy.explanation: The next heading is “The Nethinims.”
easy.q: Which group is listed after the porters?

easy.explanation: Many Nethinim families are named in the passage.
easy.q: What does the Nethinim list especially provide?

answers: They were connected with gate service
medium.explanation: Porters were associated with service at the gates.
medium.q: What can be understood from the phrase “the children of the porters”?

medium.explanation: The Nethinim were a service group connected with the Temple.
medium.q: What were the Nethinim associated with?

medium.explanation: The names preserve the identity and organization of the families.
medium.q: Why are many family names preserved?

answers: It preserves many ancient group names
challenge.explanation: The list preserves the names of these old service families.
challenge.q: What historical detail is distinctive about the Nethinim list?

answers: Both are counted as service groups
They are unrelated in the list
challenge.explanation: Both groups are presented among those serving the community and sanctuary.
challenge.q: What connection do the porters and Nethinim have in the passage?

answers: To preserve the identity of the groups
challenge.explanation: Naming the families preserves their distinct identities.
challenge.q: Why does the list retain family names instead of giving only one total?

easy.explanation: The heading says, “The children of Solomon’s servants.”
easy.q: Whose descendants are listed in this section?

easy.explanation: Several families are named, followed by a total.
easy.q: What does the section include?

answers: As members of the royal family
easy.explanation: The idea describes them as foreign servants connected with Solomon.
easy.q: How are Solomon’s servants described in the supplied idea?

answers: They are included together in the total
They have no connection in the passage
medium.explanation: The total includes both the Nethinim and Solomon’s servants’ descendants.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the Nethinim and Solomon’s servants in verse 58?

answers: Families descended from servants associated with Solomon
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies the families listed in this section.
medium.q: What does “the children of Solomon’s servants” identify?

medium.explanation: The total summarizes the Nethinim and Solomon’s servants’ descendants.
medium.q: Why is a total given at the end?

answers: The returning community included groups of varied origin
They were excluded from the return
challenge.explanation: They appear as part of the community that came up.
challenge.q: What does including Solomon’s servants’ descendants in the list show?

challenge.explanation: The passage preserves family identities and also records their combined number.
challenge.q: What does the movement from family names to a total emphasize?

challenge.explanation: Verse 58 explicitly includes the Nethinim in the total.
challenge.q: Which detail might be missed on a quick reading?

easy.explanation: They could not show whether they were of Israel.
easy.q: What could some of the people not prove?

easy.explanation: They sought their register among those reckoned by genealogy.
easy.q: What did certain priestly families seek?

answers: They were put from the priesthood
easy.explanation: They were treated as polluted and removed from the priesthood.
easy.q: What happened to those whose priestly genealogy was not found?

answers: It could establish a claim to the priesthood
medium.explanation: Genealogy was needed to verify priestly status.
medium.q: Why was the genealogical register important?

medium.explanation: It refers to being recorded according to ancestry.
medium.q: What does “reckoned by genealogy” mean?

answers: They were not to eat them until a priest arose with Urim and Thummim
They were to recount every person
medium.explanation: They had to wait until the priest could provide a proper determination.
medium.q: What did the Tirshatha command concerning the most holy things?

answers: Ancestry and priestly status had official importance
Anyone could be a priest without proof
challenge.explanation: The records were used to determine eligibility for priestly service.
challenge.q: What does the search for genealogical records reveal about the society?

answers: Uncertainty led to waiting for a proper determination
challenge.explanation: Those whose records were missing had to wait before eating the holy things.
challenge.q: What is the connection between uncertain genealogy and the temporary restriction?

challenge.explanation: The phrase directly states that the genealogical records could not be found.
challenge.q: Which phrase most clearly emphasizes that the records were missing?

paragraphs.title: The Census and Possessions of the Assembly

easy.explanation: The passage gives the number of the whole congregation.
easy.q: What is given for the whole congregation?

easy.explanation: The passage counts servants, maids, and singing men and women.
easy.q: Who else is counted besides the congregation?

easy.explanation: These four kinds of animals are counted.
easy.q: Which animals are mentioned?

answers: To show the size and possessions of the returning group
To count the cities of Judah
medium.explanation: The animals were part of the caravan and its possessions.
medium.q: Why are the animals included in the record?

medium.explanation: The possessive wording identifies the mules as part of their property.
medium.q: What does “their mules” mean?

medium.explanation: The text says, “Beside their servants and their maids.”
medium.q: How are the servants counted in relation to the congregation?

answers: It describes a whole community and its possessions
It was only a military march
challenge.explanation: The census includes the assembly, servants, singers, and livestock.
challenge.q: What does the variety of people and animals suggest about the return?

answers: They formed a distinct group within the community
challenge.explanation: The text identifies two hundred singing men and women as a separate group.
challenge.q: Why are the singers mentioned separately from the servants and maids?

answers: The asses had the largest stated number
challenge.explanation: The passage records 6,720 asses, the largest number among the listed animals.
challenge.q: Which detail is easy to miss in the animal census?

easy.explanation: Some of the chief of the fathers offered freely.
easy.q: Who offered freely for the work?

answers: To set up the house of God
To build a palace in Babylon
easy.explanation: The offerings were for the house of God in Jerusalem.
easy.q: What was the purpose of the offerings?

easy.explanation: The text names gold, silver, and one hundred priests’ garments.
easy.q: What was given for the work?

answers: Each gave according to his ability
medium.explanation: The phrase means the gifts matched the donors’ means.
medium.q: What does “they gave after their ability” mean?

answers: When they came to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Their offering occurred when they came to the Temple site in Jerusalem.
medium.q: When did the chief fathers offer freely?

answers: They were also needed for the restoration of worship
medium.explanation: The garments supported the priests’ service in the restored Temple.
medium.q: Why are priests’ garments listed with gold and silver?

answers: The return included commitment to restore the Temple
challenge.explanation: Their gifts were specifically given for the house of God.
challenge.q: What does the offering reveal about the purpose of the return?

answers: To restore the house of God to its proper place
challenge.explanation: The phrase expresses the desire to reestablish the Temple in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What does “to set it up in his place” mean?

answers: The chief fathers gave to the treasure of the work
The gifts went to a foreign king
challenge.explanation: The leaders contributed to a common treasury for the work.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the contributions were communal?

easy.explanation: The verse says they dwelt in their cities.
easy.q: Where did the returning groups dwell at the end of the chapter?

answers: Priests, Levites, singers, porters, and Nethinim
easy.explanation: The verse names these groups among those who settled.
easy.q: Which groups are named as dwelling in their cities?

easy.explanation: The verse concludes, “and all Israel in their cities.”
easy.q: Who else dwelt in the cities?

answers: The final verse describes where the listed groups settled
medium.explanation: After listing the groups, Ezra describes their settlement.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the lists and the final verse?

answers: In the cities assigned or belonging to them
medium.explanation: The phrase describes their establishment in their respective towns.
medium.q: What does “in their cities” mean?

answers: To show their distinct roles within the whole people
medium.explanation: The verse names the service groups and then includes all Israel.
medium.q: Why are special groups named before “all Israel”?

answers: A move from returning to establishing permanent life
challenge.explanation: Dwelling in the cities marks the community’s establishment in the land.
challenge.q: What does settlement in the cities symbolize?

answers: The settlement included every part of the community
challenge.explanation: The verse includes both special service groups and the entire nation.
challenge.q: What is shown by naming priests, Levites, and all Israel together?

answers: The chapter begins with return and ends with settlement
It begins with rebuilding and ends with exile
challenge.explanation: The opening describes coming back, while the ending describes dwelling in the cities.
challenge.q: What connection does the ending create with the beginning of the chapter?
